verses.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.2: You commanded the children of Israel, and you said to them, “Offer your sacrifices to Me as an offering of holiness. Let their fragrance be preserved, so that they may be offered to Me on the appointed days.”
verses.3: And you said to them, “This is the woman whom you shall present to Jehovah. She should be young girls, pure and innocent. They must be presented two days before the Sabbath.”
verses.4: You will make one of the bricks in the morning, and you will make the second brick between noon and afternoon.
verses.5: And the rich man prepared a meal for himself, in a small vessel filled with honey.
verses.6: The constant aroma of the sacrifices offered on Mount Sinai fills the air with the scent of sweet incense for Jehovah.
verses.7: And the fourth lamb was sacrificed for the one altar in the Holy Day. This sacrifice was offered as a reward for Jehovah.
verses.8: And the second incense shall be burned between the evenings, as an offering for the morning. And it shall be a fragrant offering to the LORD.
verses.9: And on the day of Shabbat, two years old children were given offerings. They were also given twelve-year-olds who prepared the offerings in the Temple.
verses.10: He ascends on the Sabbath, onto that eternal throne.
verses.11: And at the beginning of your new year, you shall offer up to Jehovah two lambs and one kid as sacrifices. These are to be offered on the seventh day of each month.
verses.12: And three dozen portions of food were given away in the wilderness, for one lamb. And two dozen portions of food were also given away in the wilderness, for one goat.
verses.13: And one hundred and ten pieces of bread were placed in the basket for the offering. The smell from those breads was pleasant to the Lord.
verses.14: And half of them will be used for meat, a third for fish, and a fourth for vegetables. This is the amount that can be used in one month, during the months of the year.
verses.15: And one wicked person will be punished for his sins against Jehovah, upon entering the eternal abyss.
verses.16: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, it was Passover for Jesus.
verses.17: And on the fifteenth day of this month, there is a seven-day holiday called “Shivat Yamim.”
verses.18: On that first day, it is a sacred day; no work shall be done at all.
verses.19: And you shall bring with you a female lamb for Yahweh. It should be two year-old lambs, along with one ewe and seven one-year-old goats. They must all be pure and healthy.
verses.20: And from their offerings, three hundred and twenty will be given to the sheep, and two hundred and twenty to the goats.
verses.21: Thirty times three will be the number of times one rod is used to make seven rods.
verses.22: And one sin will be placed upon your shoulders.
verses.23: In addition to the morning journey, those who go on a permanent journey must also do these things.
verses.24: In those days, for seven days, they shall make bread with a sweet smell for the Lord. This will be done as an offering for everlastingness.
verses.25: And on the seventh day, from the time of the call to worship, you shall not do any work.
verses.26: And on the day of sacrifice, when you offer your new offerings to Jehovah with your offerings from the time of the “Korban Kodesh,” then all your labors will be made fruitful for you. You shall not do any other work.
verses.27: And you brought up two sheep as an offering to God. They were two rams, seven heifers, and two yearlings.
verses.28: And from their offerings, three hundred and twenty were given to the first lamb; two hundred and twenty were given to the second lamb.
verses.29: Thirty for one bucket, for the seven buckets in total.
verses.30: One strong horn will be placed on your heads.
verses.31: And its ascent will be eternal, and its descent will also be eternal. It will remain pure for you, and it will be suitable for your use.
